topic.title_target: I pronomi personali soggetto e la loro omissione
learning_objectives: Identify the six grammatical persons and omit an unnecessary subject pronoun naturally.
Recognise the subject from a familiar given verb form even when the pronoun is not present.
Use an explicit subject pronoun to express a contrast or make a referent clear.
scope_included: io, tu, lui, lei, noi, voi, loro

skills.description_en: Match io, tu, lui, lei, noi, voi and loro with the relevant grammatical person and number.
Identify the person and number indicated by an example present-tense verb form.
Omit a subject pronoun when the person and referent are already clear.
Use explicit subject pronouns to contrast speakers or other people.
Choose a third-person pronoun to refer clearly to a known person or group.
Produce short natural sentences with omitted or deliberately expressed subject pronouns.

lesson.short_explanation_en: In Italian, the verb usually shows who is doing something, so you normally say Parlo italiano rather than Io parlo italiano. Use io, tu, lui, lei, noi, voi and loro to make the person clear or draw a contrast. Lui and lei share the same singular verb form, parla.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: Italian has the subject pronouns io, tu, lui, lei, noi, voi and loro. Lui and lei share the same third-person singular verb form. The verb endings normally show who is speaking or acting.
rule_blocks.pattern: io → parlo; tu → parli; lui/lei → parla; noi → parliamo; voi → parlate; loro → parlano
usage_notes_en: Use tu to speak to one person and voi to speak to more than one person in familiar contexts.
Lui and lei refer to a male and a female person respectively in the examples; their verb form is the same.
The full conjugation system is not the goal of this lesson: read the given forms to identify the subject.
common_errors_en: Incorrect: io parla italiano. Correct: parlo italiano (or io parlo italiano when emphasising the speaker).
Incorrect: loro parla italiano. Correct: loro parlano italiano.

rule_blocks.heading_en: Omit the subject when it is clear
rule_blocks.explanation_en: Italian usually does not need a subject pronoun. Use the verb alone when the person is already understood from the form or from the previous sentence.
usage_notes_en: A dropped subject is normal and complete Italian, not a missing word.
For third-person subjects, the previous sentence often identifies who the verb refers to.
An explicit pronoun is not automatically wrong; it simply has a communicative effect.
common_errors_en: Unnatural repetition: io parlo italiano. Io parlo inglese. Better when no contrast is intended: Parlo italiano. Parlo inglese.
Do not remove a subject if doing so makes the intended person unclear.

rule_blocks.heading_en: Keep pronouns for contrast or clarity
rule_blocks.explanation_en: Say io, tu, lui, lei, noi, voi or loro when you want to contrast people, emphasise a subject, or make clear who is meant. It is especially useful for lui versus lei because both use parla.
rule_blocks.pattern: Io parlo italiano, tu parli inglese. / Lui parla italiano, lei parla inglese.
usage_notes_en: Pronouns may appear for deliberate emphasis even when the verb identifies the person.
Do not treat all explicit pronouns as compulsory; use them when they help the message.
common_errors_en: Do not drop lui or lei blindly when two people are being compared and the referent could become unclear.

form_tables.title_en: Subject pronouns with example present-tense forms of parlare

rows: Io parlo italiano, tu parli inglese.
Lui parla italiano, lei parla inglese.

contexts.setting_en: Anna and Marco meet at a language class.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.translation_en: Hi, I’m Anna. I speak Italian.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Ciao, sono Marco. Io parlo inglese.
lines.translation_en: Hi, I’m Marco. I speak English.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.target: Tu parli inglese, io parlo italiano.
lines.translation_en: You speak English, and I speak Italian.

focus_items.explanation_en: The speaker is clear, so Anna does not need io.
Marco emphasises his language in contrast to Anna’s.
Anna contrasts what Marco speaks with what she speaks.
The form parliamo indicates noi without repeating it.

contexts.setting_en: Two friends use different languages while talking with family and friends.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.target: Anna è a casa. Parla con la mamma.
lines.translation_en: Anna is at home. She talks with her mother.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.target: Marco è al lavoro. Lui parla con un amico.
lines.translation_en: Marco is at work. He talks with a friend.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.target: Lei parla italiano, lui parla inglese.
lines.translation_en: She speaks Italian; he speaks English.

focus_items.explanation_en: The previous sentence names Anna, so the subject can be omitted.
Lui makes it clear that this sentence refers to Marco.
Lei and lui make a clear contrast between Anna and Marco.

examples.note_en: The speaker is clear: io is normally omitted.
Parli signals tu, even without the pronoun.

examples.target: Marco è a casa. Parla italiano.
examples.translation_en: Marco is at home. He speaks Italian.
examples.note_en: The previous sentence names Marco, so lui is unnecessary.

examples.target: Io parlo italiano, tu parli inglese.
examples.translation_en: I speak Italian; you speak English.
examples.note_en: Explicit pronouns draw a contrast between two people.

examples.target: Lui parla italiano, lei parla inglese.
examples.translation_en: He speaks Italian; she speaks English.
examples.note_en: Lui and lei distinguish two people whose verb forms match.
The ending -ate identifies voi in this present-tense example.

examples.target: Anna e Marco parlano italiano. Parlano ogni giorno.
examples.translation_en: Anna and Marco speak Italian. They speak every day.
examples.note_en: Loro is omitted because the referents are already known.

examples.target: Noi parliamo italiano, voi parlate inglese.
examples.translation_en: We speak Italian; you speak English.
examples.note_en: The explicit pronouns distinguish our group from your group.

examples.target: Loro parlano italiano, noi parliamo inglese.
examples.translation_en: They speak Italian; we speak English.
examples.note_en: Loro is helpful when two groups are contrasted.

exercises.instruction_en: Fill in the contrasting subject pronoun for the speaker. Write only the pronoun.
exercises.prompt_target: ___ parlo italiano, ma tu parli inglese.
hint_steps: The clause contrasts the speaker with the person addressed.
The first-person singular subject pronoun is io.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Expected: io. Io marks the speaker in contrast with tu.
exercises.explanation_en: Io marks the speaker in contrast with tu.

exercises.instruction_en: Complete the contrast with the subject pronoun for one person being addressed.
exercises.prompt_target: Io parlo italiano, ma ___ parli inglese.
hint_steps: The speaker is io; the other person is the listener.
Second-person singular is tu.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Expected: tu. Tu explicitly contrasts the listener with the speaker.
exercises.explanation_en: Tu explicitly contrasts the listener with the speaker.

exercises.instruction_en: Complete the contrast using the plural pronoun for people being addressed.
exercises.prompt_target: Noi parliamo italiano, ma ___ parlate inglese.
hint_steps: The first group is noi; the other group is being addressed.
Second-person plural is voi.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Expected: voi. Voi is the subject for the group being addressed.
exercises.explanation_en: Voi is the subject for the group being addressed.

exercises.instruction_en: Complete the contrast with the subject pronoun referring to Marco.
exercises.context_target: Anna parla italiano. Marco parla inglese.
exercises.prompt_target: Lei parla italiano, ma ___ parla inglese.
hint_steps: The missing pronoun refers to Marco, not Anna.
Use the masculine singular subject pronoun.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Expected: lui. The contrast is between Anna (lei) and Marco (lui).
exercises.explanation_en: The contrast is between Anna (lei) and Marco (lui).

exercises.instruction_en: Write one simple sentence with an omitted io, then one sentence contrasting io and tu.
exercises.prompt_target: io; parlare; italiano / tu; parlare; inglese
exercises.prompt_en: Use parlare and the two languages. Write complete natural Italian sentences.
hint_steps: Look at the verb form and who is being discussed.
Decide whether the pronoun is needed for contrast or can be omitted.
exercises.feedback_correct_en: Compare your answer with the rubric.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Check who is speaking and whether the subject needs emphasis.
exercises.explanation_en: The first sentence should use no explicit subject; the second should contrast io and tu.

criteria_en: The first sentence has a correct first-person singular verb and omits io.
The second sentence uses io and tu to mark a contrast.
Both sentences are idiomatic and grammatically coherent. No exact-text scoring.
rubric.example_response: Parlo italiano. Io parlo italiano, tu parli inglese.
